audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart contradicted itself and the packet. The packet levelChart is Illaoi for rows 0-5 and Skill at 2+ items; the page had Skill at rows 0/3/4 and Illaoi at row 6, while whys[6] literally reads 'Skill late'. So win[6] said Illaoi and its own why said Skill.
audit.why: 52.73% over 1849 games with a FAV tag matches an Illaoi-favoured laning phase that flattens once a fed Aatrox scales. The content whys[0..5] all already describe Illaoi winning those rows.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-5 = Illaoi, row 6 = Skill, proposed as one atomic group across both layers (phases[N].side and win[N] together).

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 and late-game spike text was built on Aatrox reviving from World Ender.
audit.why: Riot's own description of World Ender in the kit file lists fear on minions, bonus attack damage, increased healing and move speed, extended on takedown. There is no revive. The revive was the old Aatrox and it is the single biggest factual error on this page.
audit.corrected: Aatrox's level-6 spike is amplified healing plus AD, not a second life — which is exactly why Grievous Wounds has to be up BEFORE you press R, not bought after you lose the fight.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two grounding interactions that actually decide this lane were never stated.
audit.why: Infernal Chains (W, 20/18/16/14/12s) grounds, and Harsh Lesson (W, flat 4s) is a dash — chained, you cannot leap to him or away, and it is the one cooldown that stops your whole pattern. In the other direction Umbral Dash (E, 9/8/7/6/5s) is how he leaves the tentacle field, so a landed spirit matters more than a landed slam. The mirror audit (aatrox__illaoi) states the same pair from his side.
audit.corrected: Hold Harsh Lesson until after Infernal Chains has been spent, not before; land E so the spirit keeps taking tentacle damage even when Umbral Dash carries him out.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal was listed in the item block but never tied to a timing, and the content layer never mentions it at all.
audit.why: Aatrox heals off Deathbringer Stance (P), Umbral Dash (E) passive and amplified healing on World Ender (R) — three sources, all of which beat chip damage.
audit.corrected: Executioner's Calling is a lane purchase and must be completed before your first R commit.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1] is titled 'Trade into his Q sweetspots' but its body text is generic filler about burning a cooldown.
audit.why: The Darkin Blade's outer edge is where the damage and the Deathbringer healing come from; standing on the rim is the mistake, standing inside the swing is not.
audit.corrected: Body rewritten to state the rim-vs-inside rule.

edits.before: Plant tentacles before contesting anything. Identify how Aatrox contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Plant tentacles before contesting anything. His level-1 Q is slow and telegraphed, so Grasp trades start on your terms.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around World Ender's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Your window: E him as he steps to farm, then W the spirit — his Q healing cannot outpace two tentacles. Freeze and deny once ahead.

edits.before: Leap of Faith inside your tentacle field is a 1v3 button. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Aatrox's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Leap of Faith inside your field is a 1v3 button — a tentacle per champion hit. Press it on his Q commit, before Umbral Dash resets.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Aatrox carry threat 8/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Skill from here: your side-lane pattern is at full power, but Aatrox carry threat is 8/10 — close before the map decides for you.

edits.before: Aatrox wastes World Ender — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Amplified healing — get Executioner's up before you commit.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: The rim is his damage and his heal — stand inside the swing instead.

edits.before: Skill late: a fed Aatrox's R revive and Chains cleave can equalize teamfights.
edits.after: Skill late: World Ender's healing and Chains cleave can equalize teamfights.

edits.before: Your R Leap of Faith spawns a wall of tentacles; pop it when Aatrox commits his Q chain and every slam shreds him while his W Infernal Chains only pulls you deeper into your own tentacle field. His R World Ender revive is far less scary when he's already at low HP from your slams.
edits.after: Your R Leap of Faith spawns a tentacle per champion hit, so pop it as he commits his Q chain and every slam lands at once. Infernal Chains only drags you deeper into your own field. World Ender heals him harder, not longer — Executioner's is finished before you press R, never after.

edits.before: Skill: teamfight Aatrox with R + Chains can reset and cleave your whole team, so a fed Aatrox equalizes — respect his Q knockups and don't get chained into his slam angle.
edits.after: Skill: a fed Aatrox with World Ender's amplified healing cleaves teamfights, so he equalizes late — Infernal Chains grounds you out of Harsh Lesson, so hold W until after he lands it.

edits.before: With items and R up you dominate extended fights; drop your tentacle wall as he commits Q and his self-heal can't survive the slam volume, though a fed Aatrox's teamfight revive keeps late games honest.
edits.after: With items and R up you dominate extended fights; drop your tentacle wall as he commits Q and anti-heal keeps his drain from outracing the slam volume, though a fed Aatrox's World Ender keeps late games honest.

edits.before: Save W Infernal Chains to escape your E pull
edits.after: Land Infernal Chains to ground your Harsh Lesson

edits.before: Reach R World Ender to revive through your slam burst
edits.after: Reach R World Ender to heal through your slam burst

notes: Build inconsistency left alone because it is not resolvable from the kits: content spikes[2].text names 'Sundered Sky / Trinity' as the first item while full report[8] and every phases/ahead reference name Iceborn Gauntlet. One of the two is stale — the user should pick which build this page teaches. Per the description-beats-flag rule I did NOT use the 'grounding' or 'untargetable' flags the kit carries on Leap of Faith: Riot's own text says only that it damages nearby enemies and spawns a tentacle per champion hit. The mirror audits reached the same conclusion, so those two flags look like a tooltip-parsing misfire on Illaoi's R across every one of her matchups. Also: the pre-existing text asserted Aatrox's Q knockup; Riot's description in the kit only says three swings with different areas of effect and the kit carries no knockup flag, so I removed the claim rather than restate it unverified.
